description:
Edit repos/identity-vessel/src/index.ts so that revoking an API key is reflected by the key-listing endpoint.

The defect is a write-read split across two stores. The revoke handler at app.post("/v1/keys/revoke") calls revokeKey(), which is db/redis.ts revokeKey() and only does redis.setex("revoked:" + keyId, ttl, "1"). The listing handler at app.get("/v1/keys") reads SurrealDB: SELECT ... is_active ... FROM api_key, and derives status: r.is_active ? "active" : "revoked". Nothing ever sets is_active false, so a revoked key is listed as active forever.

Measured: after a successful revoke, POST /v1/keys/validate correctly returns valid:false with "API key has been revoked" (it consults Redis), while substrate-key list, run immediately and again ten seconds later, still shows that key as active. An operator following the documented revoke-then-list sequence sees "active" after a successful revoke and reasonably concludes the revoke failed.

The fix: in the revoke handler, after revokeKey() succeeds, also UPDATE the api_key row in SurrealDB to set is_active = false for the revoked key_id, using the same query helper the listing handler imports from ./db/surrealdb. Redis remains the fast path the validate route checks; SurrealDB becomes accurate rather than stale. Do not change the validate path.
